title: Third-Space Optimisation (3SO) in Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Narrative Review and Proposed Framework for Integrating the Patellofemoral Joint into Alignment Planning
content: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) planning has centred on tibiofemoral alignment and balance, with the patellofemoral joint assessed only after tibiofemoral decisions have been made. Yet anterior knee pain remains a leading contributor to dissatisfaction after TKA. This narrative review synthesises the biomechanical, imaging and clinical literature on patellofemoral mechanics in TKA (PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library; 1990–2026) and, on that basis, proposes Third-Space Optimisation (3SO): a patellofemoral constraint layer applied within any existing alignment strategy rather than a new alignment philosophy. The evidence shows that patellofemoral kinematics are sensitive to femoral axial rotation, mediolateral femoral position, tibial component orientation and implantation depth — variables that no current strategy targets collectively. Because tibiofemoral balance can be achieved through multiple component configurations, a solution space exists within which patellofemoral consequences can be weighed. We identify the anterior chamfer zone (approximately 20–60° of flexion) as an intraoperative blind spot and argue that the distal femoral morphotype, rather than global limb alignment, may drive patellofemoral risk. Patellar resurfacing cannot compensate for suboptimal component positioning. A descriptive stepwise pathway and a research agenda are presented. The framework is hypothesis-generating; prospective studies with standardised patellofemoral kinematic endpoints are required for validation.
